II |publisher = [[Universidad de Buenos Aires]] |pages = 184, 188 |language = Spanish |url-status = dead |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20071213194657/http://www.darwin.edu.ar/Publicaciones/CatalogoVascII/CatalogoVascII.asp |archive-date = 13 December 2007 |df = dmy-all }}| }} '''''Senecio brasiliensis''''', known by the [[common name]] '''flor-das-almas''' (flower-of-souls), is a perennial species of the family [[Asteraceae]]. It is native to fields and meadows of central South America. ==Description== ''S. brasiliensis'' is a densely leafy [[perennial]] herb, {{convert|1|m|ft}} to {{convert|2|m|ft}} tall, with yellow flowers that prefers to make its home in degraded [[pasture]] lands and unploughed [[cropland]]s in central South America.{{Cite journal | url = https://www.uepg.br/propesp/publicatio/exa/2005_3/06.pdf | title = Entomofauna associada ao ''Senecio brasiliensis'' Less (Asteraceae), e ''Phaedon confinis'' (Insecta; Coleoptera; Chrysomelidae) como possível agente controlador desta planta tóxica |trans-title=Entomofauna associated with ''Senecio brasiliensis'' Less (Asteraceae), and ''Phaedon Confinis'' (Insecta; Coleoptera; Chrysomelidae) as a possible controller agent of this toxic plant | access-date = 5 March 2008 |author1=Michelli Maria Mendes |author2=Maysa de Lima Leite |author3=Geovan Henrique Corrêa |author4=Julianne Milléo | authorlink = Universidade Estadual de Ponta Grossa | date = 2005-04-20 | journal = Publicatio UEPG: Ciências Exatas e da Terra, Agrárias e Engenharias |volume=11 |issue=3 |pages=45–53 |hdl=123456789/625 | language = pt | quote = ''Phaedon confinis'' Klug, 1829 (Chrysomelidae) was the one that most stood out, specially because it was found in great numbers on the plant }}{{Cite web|url=http://www.vet.uga.edu/VPP/NSEP/toxic_plants/POR/Senecio/index.htm |title=''Senecio'' spp. |access-date=2008-03-05 |author1=Claudio Barros |author2=Elissa Totin |author3=Raquel Rech |author4=Marcia Ilha |author5=Steve Valeika |authorlink=Universidade Federal de Santa Maria |date=March 2001 |work=Lista de Plantas |publisher=[[Universidade Federal de Santa Maria]] |language=pt |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080221081205/http://www.vet.uga.edu/VPP/nsep/toxic_plants/POR/Senecio/index.htm |archive-date=21 February 2008 }} '''Leaves and stems''': ''S. brasiliensis'' stands very upright with a branched hairless and grooved stem. The leaves are alternate, pinnate and deeply lobed dark green on the top, whitish green on the underside.{{Cite web | url = http://www.cit.rs.gov.br/v2/nova/?p=p_126 | title = ''Senecio brasiliensis'' Less. – Maria-mole | access-date = 6 March 2008 | author = Centro de Informação Toxicológica do Rio Grande do Sul | language = pt }} The lower part of the plant is smooth, while the upper part is hairy and the leaves cluster at the highest point with the flower stalks (corymbs). '''Flowers''': Yellow flowers dense on corymbs; two types of flowers (that look like [petal]s), disc florets with both male and female flowers and ray flowers which are simply female. '''Seeds''': Small seed with white hairs that use the wind to get around with. ==Common names== *{{langx|en|Flower of souls, hempleaf ragwort}} *{{langx|pt|malmequer-amarelo, Maria-mole, tasneirinha, flor-das-almas}}{{Cite web | url = https://plants.usda.gov/index.html | title = PLANTS Profile, ''Senecio cannabinifolius'' Hook. & Arn. | access-date = 6 March 2008 | author = Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) | authorlink = Natural Resources Conservation Service | work = The PLANTS Database | publisher = [[United States Department of Agriculture]] }} *[[Guarani language|Guarani]]: ''Agosto poty'' (August flower) Image:Senecio brasiliensis.png ==Distribution== ''S. brasiliensis'' grows at elevations of 0 to {{convert|1000|m|ft}}. '''Native''': [[Argentina]] (mostly North [[Argentine Northwest]] and [[Gran Chaco]]), [[Bolivia]], [[Brazil]] (mostly [[Regions of Brazil|South Central]]), [[Paraguay]], and [[Uruguay]].
